title: Registers and Macros
description: Named and appending registers, pasting from Insert mode, and macros: record once, replay anywhere.

intro: Vim has many clipboards, called registers, each named by a letter. "a before a yank or a delete puts the text in register a, and "a before p puts it back. A capital letter appends instead of replacing, so "A can collect lines from all over a file.
A macro is keys recorded into a register. qa starts recording into a, q stops, and @a plays the keys back. An edit you can make once, the same way, can be repeated on every line that needs it.

commands.text: Use register a for the next yank, delete or put: "ayy, then "ap.
Append to register a instead of replacing it.
In Insert mode, insert a register's contents: <C-r>a, or <C-r>" for the last yank.
Start recording into a register: qa records into a. Press q again to stop.
Play a macro back: @a, or 3@a three times. @@ repeats the last one played.
Record the edit for one line, ending with j so the macro leaves the cursor on the next line, ready to run again.
A macro stops at the first key that fails, such as a search with no more matches. So a generous count is safe: 99@a runs until there's nothing left to do.

levels.title: Collector
levels.description: Gather every TODO line under '## Collected', in order, without losing the originals.
levels.hint: "ayy yanks into register a; "Ayy (capital) appends to it. Find TODOs with / and n, then "ap pastes them all at once.

levels.title: Paste while typing
levels.description: Finish the line. Register a already holds the address, so don't type it.
levels.hint: In Insert mode, <C-r> followed by a register name inserts that register.

levels.title: Record and replay
levels.description: Put a colon after every name. Do it once while recording, then replay.
levels.hint: qa starts recording into register a and q stops. Leave the cursor where the next line starts, then 5@a replays it five times.

levels.title: CSV to Lua
levels.description: Turn every CSV row into a Lua table entry. Typing it seven times is how carpal tunnel starts.
levels.hint: Record one row's edit, finishing with j to move down. I inserts at the start, f, finds the comma, cl changes it, A appends.

levels.title: Until it stops
levels.description: Delete every DEBUG line. You don't need to count them: a macro stops as soon as a step fails.
levels.hint: Record: search for the next DEBUG, delete the line, step up a line (so back-to-back DEBUG lines aren't skipped). Then replay with a generous count.
